title: Bittensor Daily News — October 27, 2026
summary: Harnyx connects research miners to REAX decision models; Beam publishes Bittensor EVM delivery receipts; Taoswap announces an Ethereum bridge; and Chutes lays out its next compute strategy. Also: a working Desearch Reddit demo, owner-key and identity changes, allocations, burns and operator updates.

ecosystem.headline: Taoswap announces a Bittensor–Ethereum bridge
ecosystem.summary: Taoswap’s October 26 announcement says users can route Ethereum USDC or ETH into TAO or subnet tokens, and convert TAO back to USDC or ETH, powered by tao.com. It offers another entry route into subnet markets. This is a team-reported product availability announcement: this review did not execute a bridge transfer, audit the bridge’s security, or verify volume and settlement performance.
ecosystem.ratingReason: A material new access route for the ecosystem, qualified to the launch evidence actually reviewed.

ecosystem.headline: Runtime 486 is finalized; the reviewed delta concerns stake availability reads
ecosystem.summary: The daily scan observes finalized runtime 486. The reviewed release source updates weight handling for stake-availability reads; this review does not claim a new allocation or burn rule from the version number alone. The collectors retained runtime-specific event layouts across the window rather than silently decoding every block with a single version.
ecosystem.ratingReason: A verified protocol-version observation with a bounded source interpretation.

updates.headline: DaniLabs sets an owner operating hotkey
updates.summary: The reviewed daily event scan records a successful SubnetOwnerHotkeySet for SN2 at block 9,369,802, extrinsic 8. This changes an operating hotkey; it is not a coldkey sale, new registration or proof of transferred business ownership. The permanent evidence includes the execution event and runtime layout.
updates.ratingReason: Verified dated team follow-up or finalized technical housekeeping; no unsupported business outcome inferred.

updates.headline: Vanta records a qualifying 103.438971428-alpha transaction burn
updates.summary: A successful SN8 AlphaBurned event at block 9,373,978 destroyed 103.438971428 alpha on October 27 at 08:55:24 UTC. The event is retained in the public burn archive with its account, transaction and historical registration label. This is a subnet burn by the recorded wallet; it is not automatically an owner-wallet burn. No additional qualifying burn was found in the subsequent fully scanned increment through the daily cutoff.
updates.ratingReason: A verified transaction burn above the individual 100-alpha threshold; no emissions withholding or pooled cross-subnet totals substituted.

updates.headline: 404—GEN delays its competition wrap-up while API work continues
updates.summary: The October 27 brief says the final Competition 3 update is delayed while API work remains unfinished, with a further update expected rather than completed. This is a schedule/operations item, not a product launch or independently validated model result.
updates.ratingReason: A routine competition delay, kept below the major-news threshold.

updates.headline: Desearch’s Reddit demo returns public discussion threads
updates.summary: Desearch announced its Reddit Search demo on October 27. Our Bittensor topic test returned ten public thread links with subreddit names and titles. The published example uses one web search restricted to Reddit; it does not read complete threads or generate an analysis, and dates may be absent. Alongside its October 26 RAG extraction example, it shows developers a small, reproducible discovery workflow rather than a claim of fresh or authoritative Reddit coverage.
updates.ratingReason: A working, inspected developer tool with limited scope; no unsupported adoption claim.

updates.headline: SN34’s finalized identity is now Yugos
updates.summary: At finalized block 9,375,531, SN34’s owner-submitted identity reads Yugos and points to the BitMind-AI/yugos repository, describing decision models for inference. This is a verified identity observation, not proof of an ownership sale or a new registration. Older BitMind stories keep their historical label. The current brief and code also discuss evaluation and sandbox restoration; these should be assessed as current Yugos work.
updates.ratingReason: A verified identity clarification that prevents readers carrying an older product label into current coverage.

updates.headline: SN36 changes its owner-submitted display name
updates.summary: The finalized identity at block 9,375,531 names SN36 “Bittensor,” replacing the Epago label seen in earlier coverage. Its accompanying description is owner-submitted commentary, not an assessment endorsed by this publication. A name edit alone does not establish a sale, new registration, partnership or change to the Bittensor network itself.
updates.ratingReason: Identity housekeeping, with the potentially confusing display name explicitly separated from the network.

updates.headline: Score removes problematic evaluation cases and reports an outage
updates.summary: Score’s October 27 brief describes blacklist/ground-truth corrections in its petrol-PPE evaluation and a Beverage service interruption. A published blacklist commit supports ongoing maintenance, but this review did not reproduce the incident or audit scores. Miners should use the current operator guidance; removed cases do not establish a general model-performance gain.
updates.ratingReason: Operational relevance for participants; competition and incident details stay attributed.

updates.headline: Nepher reports Phase 1 navigation results in simulation
updates.summary: Nepher’s October 27 update reports 76 submissions from 27 participants in its Unitree Go2 LiDAR challenge and a best reported score of 0.9272. The evaluation concerns unseen mazes in Isaac Lab. These are competition results in simulation, not a demonstrated production deployment on physical robots; the practical question is how later stages generalize beyond that test.
updates.ratingReason: Routine competition results capped at three stars, with simulation and physical deployment kept distinct.

updates.headline: Synth adds Bybit perpetual trade data to its Ultra feed
updates.summary: The October 27 operator brief says Synth Ultra adds a 60-second Bybit USDT perpetual trade stream under other_venues.bybit_futures.trades, with schema version 6. Consumers need to check schema handling rather than assume the existing parser covers the new venue. The brief says miner burn settings are unchanged; that is not an on-chain transaction-burn announcement.
updates.ratingReason: An actionable data/schema update, attributed to the operator brief.

updates.headline: Today’s Shizzy interview: Yanez and action-bound identity
updates.summary: The Yanez interview with Jose Caldera is scheduled for October 27 at 12:30 PM ET / 9:30 AM PT. Yanez’s October 26 explanation says Pulse approval binds a specific action to the owner’s live-face verification and that moment. The stream is upcoming at this report’s cutoff, not a replay or independent security audit.
updates.ratingReason: Shizzy video/interview coverage is three stars under the owner’s current rubric.

updates.headline: NIOME schedules the first stage of its GENOME migration
updates.summary: NIOME’s October 26 post puts the first 5% stage of its GENOME-on-Base to locked SN55 NIOME migration two days later, October 28. Treat this as a scheduled migration, not completed token delivery. Separately, the October 27 brief reports task-generator recovery and testnet work. Holders should distinguish the announced schedule from an executed, independently checked migration.
updates.ratingReason: A dated holder-facing plan and operational update; execution remains unconfirmed.

updates.headline: Chutes outlines off-subnet inference and a broader compute roadmap
updates.summary: Jon Durbin’s October 26 roadmap separates some additional inference options, which he says are not funded by subnet emissions, from the subnet’s incentive work. Proposed next steps include private TEE jobs, hourly GPU/CPU compute and training or serving on participants’ hardware. He explicitly says secure TEE inference and GPUs continue. These are plans and strategic direction, not evidence that all listed products have launched or become profitable.
updates.ratingReason: A consequential operating and incentive strategy from the project lead; clearly labelled as a roadmap.

updates.headline: Harnyx connects SN67 research miners to REAX decision models
updates.summary: Harnyx announced on October 27 that its research miners can now call decision models from REAX, SN92. Its published integration adds Fast and Pro providers for the smaller routing and stopping decisions inside a research run. This is a concrete connection between two subnet products; it does not establish the number of paying users, actual cost savings or independently measured research quality.
updates.ratingReason: A documented cross-subnet product integration with an immediately usable role, rather than a competition result.

updates.headline: Leadpoet interview remains scheduled for October 28
updates.summary: Leadpoet’s interview is still scheduled for October 28 at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Its watch page is an upcoming broadcast, so it stays out of completed-video coverage. Current repository changes tighten arena readiness/release checks; those commits alone do not establish a new product launch.
updates.ratingReason: A verified upcoming Shizzy stream; no premature replay or launch claim.

updates.headline: SN73 changes from Parked to Elenost and adopts a 33% / 6% / 61% split
updates.summary: SN73’s owner-submitted identity changed from Parked to Elenost. A separate successful allocation event at block 9,372,736 changes owner/validator/miner proportions from 18%/41%/41% to 33%/6%/61%. The archive preserves the exact five-slot raw vectors, block hash and extrinsic. These are allocations, not a promise of a particular validator APY. Root baseline/cap treatment and observed yield can differ or lag; the split is not an alpha burn.
updates.ratingReason: A verified economic allocation change; historical labels and exact chain evidence preserved.

updates.headline: Umi describes a C6 rerun with a larger hidden evaluation set
updates.summary: Umi’s October 27 brief describes rerunning C6 against a larger hidden set after concerns about evaluation coverage and memorization. Published code also bounds retained reward coverage at successor activation. The reported future emission increase is a plan, not verified new yield. No individual miner is accused here, and evaluation concerns are not treated as proof of misconduct.
updates.ratingReason: A material evaluation/process correction, with allegations and planned economics carefully qualified.

updates.headline: KubeTEE publishes its attestation specification and records a model withdrawal
updates.summary: KubeTEE’s published repository changes add an attestation specification/schema and record withdrawal of GLM-5.3-Flash. Related documentation clarifies publication status and key-distribution assumptions. This is evidence of published engineering material, not a finding that all east–west security goals are deployed or independently audited. Operators should check the actual supported model list before relying on an older availability claim.
updates.ratingReason: A substantive compatibility and security-documentation update, without turning a specification into a completed deployment.

updates.headline: REAX plans a 10% miner-budget burn from October 30; inference share falls from 50% to 40%
updates.summary: REAX’s announcement, pictured in Shizzy’s October 26 post and corroborated by the dated operator brief, schedules the inference share of its miner reward budget to fall from 50% to 40% after the October 30 engine slot. The freed 10 percentage points of that miner budget are to be burned; this is not a claim that 10% of all subnet emissions or existing holder balances are destroyed. The team says future inference rewards will follow measured customer demand, while its two competitions keep their full rewards for now. This is a planned emission mechanism, not a completed transaction burn or an already-executed change to the five-slot eTAO vector. Separately, Harnyx announced REAX provider support, and the operator brief reports early GPU-cap activation with validator 1.2.0rc11.post7.1.
updates.ratingReason: Useful adoption and operator detail; routine caps and planned reward changes remain three stars.

sources.label: Shizzy post with the team announcement image

updates.headline: Ingot corrects its q2 label to 1.75-bit and publishes format work
updates.summary: Ingot’s repository changes label the q2 round as 1.75-bit rather than 2-bit and add publication work for related GGUF outputs. The precision distinction matters when comparing model size and benchmark claims. Code publication does not independently establish model quality or availability of every output.
updates.ratingReason: A meaningful correction to a technical comparison; no unverified performance uplift asserted.

updates.headline: Last night: SN98 NeverPlayAlone changed its allocation to 33% owner, 7% validators and 60% miners
updates.summary: Carried forward from the October 26 edition so today’s morning report includes the overnight change: A successful finalized transaction at block 9,371,009 on October 26 at 23:01:36 UTC changes the five-slot allocation from 0% burn / 0% recycle / 18% owner / 41% validators / 41% miners to approximately 0% / 0% / 33% / 7% / 60%. This increases both the owner and miner shares while reducing the validator bucket. Root receives its live baseline first, capped by that validator allocation; alpha validators share any remainder. These are allocation weights, not guaranteed individual returns, and historical yield estimates can lag the change. Exact vectors, successful execution and historical registration identity are retained in the evidence.
updates.ratingReason: A finalized reward-allocation change affects subnet participants without establishing a new product or promising individual yield.

sources.label: Exact event, storage and registration evidence

updates.headline: SN103 changes from Unknown to Terza Inference; owner coldkey migrated
updates.summary: SN103’s finalized owner-submitted identity changed from unnamed (displayed as Unknown) to Terza Inference, a project describing an AI inference marketplace on Bittensor. The identity update is at block 9,375,503, extrinsic 29. Earlier on October 27, a successful ColdkeySwapped event at block 9,374,413, extrinsic 31, migrated the owner address from 5FHb1T…uPzXz to 5HZJ7Q…PweAN. The reviewed registration block remains unchanged. These are verified identity and owner-key events; they do not establish a sale price, independently tested marketplace availability or paying customer usage.
updates.ratingReason: A verified ownership/identity development, without inventing a sale or carrying old-project returns into a new claim.

updates.headline: Beam publishes Bittensor EVM receipts for transfers and Room deliveries
updates.summary: Beam announced its Bittensor EVM receipt integration on October 26. Its documentation identifies a mainnet contract and lets organizations record transfer or Room-delivery metadata, with file payloads staying off-chain. The important limit: these are reports written by Beam’s relay, not independent proof that content is correct; some Room receipts can include recipients’ signatures. This gives applications a documented way to read completion evidence from a contract, without proving that every proposed payment workflow is already deployed.
updates.ratingReason: A documented mainnet integration with clear trust limits and an application use case.

updates.headline: Minos follows up on its Montreal genetics appearance
updates.summary: In an October 26 post, Minos thanks the American Society of Human Genetics and describes sharing its genomic-AI work in Montreal. Its attached graphic explicitly identifies ASHG 2026. This is a team-reported follow-up to the earlier scheduled appearances, recovered in the seven-day overlap because it fell just before the previous report cutoff. It does not independently establish exact session times, new laboratory customers, or an investment or commercial partnership with OpenAI.
updates.ratingReason: Verified dated team follow-up or finalized technical housekeeping; no unsupported business outcome inferred.

updates.headline: SOMA reports Claude Code support and more model options
updates.summary: SOMA’s October 26 update reports Claude Code support and additional models, plus an increase in its measured token savings from 30% to 40% after its first Jev round. The savings figure is the team’s own claim, with no independent workload comparison performed here. Model availability and compression quality should be checked for the intended task; a token reduction alone does not establish equal answer quality or a universal bill reduction.
updates.ratingReason: A useful product update, with performance claims kept attributed rather than promoted as verified benchmarks.

updates.headline: Ditto reports evaluation changes and a withholding split
updates.summary: Ditto’s October 27 brief reports evaluation wording changes and a 15% generator/35% agent split with 50% withheld from epoch 25,962. That wording concerns the incentive mechanism; this edition does not count it as a qualifying transaction burn. The next integration version is discussed as work in progress.
updates.ratingReason: A useful operator/evaluation change; withholding is explicitly excluded from transaction-burn totals.

updates.headline: Attelier describes a staged video-inference bootstrap
updates.summary: Attelier’s October 27 brief describes a permissioned video-inference bootstrap, a provider-application window and a later gateway step. It says weights are not yet active and trace verification remains work in progress. These are staged rollout plans, not a completed open network or measured customer deployment.
updates.ratingReason: A potentially material rollout, accurately kept developing until the activation evidence exists.

Discord briefs are attributed secondary summaries; private original messages and reported miner incidents were not independently audited. Those stories remain developing.

Team performance, customer-spend and savings claims were not independently benchmarked or reconciled against private billing. No bridge transaction or paid compute workload was executed for this review.
Not every full-length media attachment or interview was watched. Text-only and media-access limits are recorded in the source audit.

Earlier burn history retains its disclosed indexer/history limits. New contiguous finalized reviews end at the stated block; miner emissions, withholding, fees and recycling are not transaction burns.
